const b="/Users/jamie/development/exposed.rankings-page";
const report=`# Rankings page design sketch

## Product and route

Add a real \`/rankings\` route and a primary landing-page link. Keep one rankings page with one compact category wheel and one top-ten list. The wheel options are MPs, Individuals, Companies, and Parties. Selecting an option replaces the list and applies that category's accent. Use an 800px page column and a 38px heading. Do not add explanatory subheadings, “All records”, replay, or “Show more”.

Use a native radio group (or buttons with \`aria-pressed\`) for the wheel. Each option needs a text label and a non-color selected marker such as a checked icon, dot, or inset border; selected state also changes border and tinted surface. MPs use the existing purple accent; the other three use the funder teal/green accent. Keep focus styling on the neutral focus token. Animate list-row entry/selection with a short opacity/translate transition; put the transition behind \`prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference\` and render the same settled list with reduced motion. Ensure keyboard selection works without requiring pointer use. The rank number remains text, so order is not communicated by color.

## Domain ownership and service shape

Introduce a rankings domain model and service alongside entity details:

\`\`\`rust
pub enum RankingCategory { Members, Individuals, Companies, Parties }
pub struct RankingsRequest { pub category: RankingCategory }
pub struct RankingEntry {
    pub rank: NonZeroUsize,
    pub id: RankingEntityId,
    pub name: String,
    pub declared_gbp: Option<BigDecimal>,
    pub incomplete: bool,
    pub declaration_count: usize,
}
pub struct Rankings { pub category: RankingCategory, pub entries: Vec<RankingEntry> }

pub trait RankingsService: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn top_ten(&self, request: RankingsRequest)
      -> impl Future<Output = Result<Rankings, RankingsError>> + Send;
}
\`\`\`

Use an exhaustive \`RankingEntityId\` enum carrying \`MemberId\`, \`FunderId\`, or \`PartyId(i32)\`; do not pass category/id combinations as strings. The response wire DTO serializes money as decimal text (never floating-point JSON), and represents an absent amount separately from zero. Reuse the existing JSON conventions for exact BigDecimal output and expose only fields the list needs. Ranking order is descending known exact GBP total, then normalized display name and stable ID; assign ranks after sorting and truncate to ten in the service.

Keep category inclusion in the domain vocabulary: \`DeclarationCategory::DonationSupport\` is source category 3 and includes loans/support. Funder eligibility is an exhaustive match on parsed \`FunderKind\`: only \`Individual\` enters Individuals and only \`Company\` enters Companies. Resolve a queried funder to its persisted canonical alias group first, then sum all member funder IDs in that group once. The group identity is already the canonical representation used by funder details; do not recreate alias matching in the ranking query. Parties are aggregated by each member's latest stored \`party_id/party_name\`, using the member's category-3 declarations; they are not inferred from funder \`RegisteredParty\` identities or direct party donations.

### Shared current-term rule

The current-term cutoff and incomplete GBP semantics currently live in private \`PeriodAggregate\` and \`CurrentParliamentStart\` in \`domain/services/entity_details.rs\`. Extract the reusable owner to \`domain/models/declared_gbp.rs\` (or a narrowly named shared aggregation module): a typed \`CurrentParliamentStart\` with the existing 2024-07-09T00:00:00Z constant and \`includes(Option<DateTime<Utc>>)\\`, plus \`DeclaredGbpPeriodAggregate\` that observes declaration count and entry values across *all* categories. It should preserve current behavior: current-term totals include registrations at or after cutoff; undated declarations are historical only; GBP sums remain exact; null currency and missing GBP amount mark totals incomplete; known non-GBP currencies do not contribute to GBP or make it incomplete; null differs from zero.

Refactor the existing entity-details \`PeriodAggregate::gbp_total\` path to call this shared accumulator for historical and current-term totals, so the existing backend member summary remains authoritative. Rankings should consume the same accumulator/rule. This is a targeted extraction; leave the member currency/category breakdown and calendar-year aggregation in entity details.

## Read path and API

Add \`rankings\` to \`domain::repositories\`, \`domain::services\`, HTTP state/server construction, and route \`GET /rankings?category=members|individuals|companies|parties\`. Parse the query string once into the closed \`RankingCategory\` enum and return a bad-request response for unknown categories. Add one endpoint that returns one selected board; the page needs only its active category and this avoids sending four sets on every initial render.

Implement \`RankingsRepo::top_ten(category, current_term_start)\` over one read-only repeatable-read transaction and a bounded set of SQLx macro queries (one selected-board aggregate query, possibly one lookup CTE/read for group resolution if combined query shape becomes unclear). No query per candidate. Keep response construction and error mapping in the service. Queries must return exact PostgreSQL NUMERIC/BigDecimal, counts, and completeness inputs, then the domain accumulator/sort owns semantics. Use \`query!\`/\`query_as!\` macros and update checked-in SQLx metadata. A single grouped query per selected board is the preferred efficient shape; it can join members, declarations, entries, and funders, group by the relevant entity, and use CTEs for alias-group canonical IDs. For MP category, aggregate all declaration categories and separate historical/current-term contributions. For the three support boards filter with \`category_id = 3\`, and for company/individual apply parsed canonical funder kind in the repository mapping; for parties group on current \`members.party_id\` and label from the latest \`members.party_name\`.

To avoid a second definition of the cutoff, pass the typed cutoff timestamp from the service/repository request as a SQL parameter rather than embedding another date literal in SQL. Prefer returning aggregate components (known GBP sum, declaration count, unknown-currency count, GBP missing-amount count) so the shared domain accumulator constructs the same completeness rule. The repository can return more than ten candidates because ordering/truncation should happen after exact typed aggregation; it must not limit before grouping or use floating point. If table size makes full exact sorting material, keep the grouped query on the DB and use exact \`NUMERIC DESC\` ordering with deterministic name/id tiebreaks and LIMIT 10, while preserving shared semantics through a typed aggregate result constructor and tests that compare it with the shared member-summary accumulator.

### Transport and frontend

Add \`/rankings\` to the Svelte route matcher/page model and page presentation. The \`+page.server.ts\` load fetches the Rust API through existing server helper/config (\`EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN\` stays server-side), validates response shape and decimal strings, then passes a typed serializable \`RankingsPageModel\` to the component. No browser API fetch, client recomputation, amount conversion, or fallback sum. Amount formatting is a feature adapter that formats decimal strings without JavaScript \`Number\`; display the declared amount label/wording if a label is needed and preserve null/incomplete state.

Suggested components: feature-owned \`RankingsPage.svelte\` owns selected category, URL, list layout, and CSS; a \`RankingWheel.svelte\` can be feature-local unless the pattern is truly reused. Each row is a native list item and links to member/funder detail; party rows may link to a filtered search only if such a real destination exists, otherwise remain text. The selected category controls the page accent variable and visible selection indicator. Page list updates should preserve focus on the selected wheel option; don't move focus to the first result automatically.

LandingPage adds a “Rankings” ButtonLink in its existing navigation. Add only this requested visible label. The UI reference favors native structures, typed presentation props, shared tokens, and feature-owned arrangement, so no generic UI component is needed for this first use.

## Rejected alternative

Do not build four separate routes or have the browser request/recalculate all boards. Four endpoints duplicate navigation and page state; browser aggregation would violate server-only data loading and exact money constraints. A single endpoint returning all categories would be workable but does unnecessary work on initial load and complicates selecting category-specific eligibility. A database-only SUM implementation with its own hard-coded date and null rules is also rejected because it would create a second owner alongside entity-details totals.

## Risks / decisions to preserve

- Ranking semantics are declared support amounts, not earnings. The company/individual/party boards use category 3 (including loans and other support), while the MP board uses totals across all declaration categories as required by its current summary rule.
- Ranking by known GBP sum when \`incomplete\` is true can place a partially-known entity alongside a complete one. Keep the completeness flag in the API and UI presentation model; if product later chooses to exclude incomplete rows, treat that as a semantic change requiring authorization.
- Funder aliases may contain conflicting kinds. The persisted canonical group name/kind should be selected using the existing representative policy, or ambiguity should be rejected/omitted explicitly; do not silently let any group member's kind qualify the whole group. Confirm and test this mapping during implementation.
- Latest party name/id may vary across members within a party due to source drift. Group by \`party_id\` and select a deterministic latest/current label; consider reporting inconsistent labels as an ingestion/data-quality case rather than splitting one party ranking.
- SQLx compile verification requires a configured database or the project's checked-in \`.sqlx\` metadata workflow. The query plan must account for this before implementation.
`;

content.text: Design report saved to `/tmp/exposed-ranking-design-luna.md`. It includes the proposed UI, typed backend and API shape, shared totals rules, read path, and risks. I flagged one open choice for the parent: whether the MP board ranks current-term or historical totals.
